issued_at: 11:00 am, 03 September 2026 (Valid for broadcast until the next advisory to be issued at ) PILANDOK HAS EXITED THE PHILIPPINE AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS Heavy Rainfall Outlook Refer to Weather Advisory No. 47 issued at 11:00 AM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to the Southwest Monsoon. Severe Winds The Southwest Monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds): Today until Saturday (05 September): Most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental. HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters: Up to 4.0 m: The western and southern seaboards of Batanes; the western seaboard of Babuyan Islands; the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte; Up to 3.5 m: The remaining seaboards of Batanes and Ilocos Norte; the seaboards of Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Zambales; the western seaboard of Pangasinan; the western and southern seaboards of Bataan; the northern and western seaboards Lubang Islands; the northwestern seaboard of Occidental Mindoro. Up to 3.0 m: The remaining seaboards of Babuyan Islands; the western seaboards of Cavite, Batangas, northern Occidental Mindoro; the northwestern seaboards of Calamian Islands, and Kalayaan Islands. Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels. Up to moderate seas over the following coastal waters: Up to 2.5 m: The seaboard of Isabela, northern Aurora, Surigao del Sur, and Davao Oriental; the western seaboard of northern Palawan; the remaining seaboards of Kalayaan Islands, Occidental Mindoro, and Pangasinan. Up to 2.0 m: The seaboards of Cagayan, Romblon, Cuyo Islands, Cagayancillo Islands, and Antique; the southern seaboards of Quezon, Marinduque, Camarines Sur, Iloilo, and Guimaras; the eastern and southern seaboards of Oriental Mindoro; the western seaboard of southern Negros Occidental; the remaining western seaboard of mainland Palawan; the remaining seaboards of Occidental Mindoro. Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions. Other coastal waters have forecast wave heights of less than 2.0 m. TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK Outside the PAR, PILANDOK will continue moving generally northwestward towards southern Japan. Beginning tomorrow (04 September) until Sunday (06 September), it will remain almost stationary then move generally southward, looping over the area of Okinawa-Amami islands. By Monday (07 September), it will move generally southeastward before turning northeastward by Tuesday (08 September). PILANDOK is forecast to remain as a tropical storm throughout the entire forecast period.
